memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Put limits for the people around the mountain and tell them, 'Be careful that
you do not approach the mountain or touch the foot of it. Whoever touches the
mountain is to be put to death. They are to be stoned or shot with arrows; not a
hand is to be laid on them. No person or animal shall be permitted to live.'
Only when the ram's horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain."
- Ex 19:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is severe, and we should not soften it.

A boundary is drawn around the mountain, and crossing it means death. Even the
method is specified so that no one else is endangered by touching the offender.

Why so extreme? Because God is holy, and holiness is not a mood. It is a reality
as genuine as fire. You do not walk into a furnace casually because you feel
sincere about it.

We live in a time that finds this difficult. We are comfortable with God as
loving and forgiving, and less comfortable with a God whose presence is
dangerous. But Scripture holds both, and a God who was only approachable would
not be worth approaching.

Here is what makes this chapter so important for Christians. Hebrews deliberately
contrasts Sinai with what believers have come to: "You have not come to a
mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire... But you have come
to Mount Zion... to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant" (Heb 12:18-24).

The boundary was real. And in Christ, the curtain has been torn (Matt 27:51).
The God who could not be approached has made a way to be approached.

Do not lose either half of that.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your view of God missing His holiness or His welcome?
2. What does it cost God that you may now come near?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Holy God, You are not safe or small. Thank You that through Jesus I may come
near to the One I could never approach on my own. Amen.
